chapter: Reel 2: Crescendo Club and Good Hearts
title: Mamie Smith's burial and her recordings of his songs
summary: The Good Hearts paid for Mamie Smith's burial when those who profited from her did not; late in life she recorded songs by Johnson and Andy Razaf.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: I think that's wonderful -- artists helping their fellow artists. And I remember reading an article, in fact, that said it was because of the Good Hearts Welfare Association that Mamie Smith got a decent burial. Could you tell us a little about that?

That's correct -- because the people who profited most from Mamie Smith and her success, full days they had nothing to bury her with when she died. And we had taken care of her immediate needs through our association, the Good Hearts, the welfare association, we had taken care of her immediate needs, and when she died, we buried her. And there was no one else to do anything about it; no one came up and said, "Here's $100 toward the burial" that I can remember -- every dime that we used came out of the Treasury.
JC, did Mamie Smith record any of your songs?

Yes, she did. In later years, she recorded songs of mine before, it would have been impossible for her to do when she was with Perry Bradford, because he was sitting in the driver's seat, and anything that she recorded, it would either be his or a part of his. So now that she belonged to our organization, and she wanted to record before she cut out for the green land, why, she recorded a couple of Andy Razaf and my songs.
Uh huh. I understand there was
a tremendous funeral for her, that people converged on the place from all over.

Yes. You're right there. And a funny thing -- those who made the most money with her had nothing to do with her burial. They didn't contribute a dime toward burying Mamie-- we did. The Good Hearts Welfare Association organized, just for the purpose of helping people like Mamie Smith.
You know, it is ironic, but you know, we've talked about it so many times, JC, whatever you give out in life, it comes back to you. A hundred fold.
